Re: PEBB Insurance Tier Ratios

The Affordable Care Act contains language regarding an excise tax to be levied on plans exceeding a maximum premium threshold in 2018. Due to PEBB's current tier ratios, PEBB is at risk of paying an excise tax should this portion of the ACA go into effect as planned.

PEBB can mitigate the risk of paying an excise tax by adjusting the tier ratios to be more in line with the ACA tier ratios. This will increase the premiums for the employee, spouse and children tier, while lowering the premiums in the other tiers. It is PEBB's intention to adjust the tier ratios as described above to avoid payment of an excise tax beginning with the 2017 plan.

As PEBB adjusts the tier ratios in 2017, PEBB intends to ease the burden of this transition for the members impacted by these changes by subsidizing the increase in premium share for employees enrolled in the employee, spouse and children tier. This will be done in such a way that these employees would pay no more in premium share than if the tier ratios were the same in the 2017 plan year as in the 2016 plan year. The subsidy would continue for the 2017 and 2018 plan years, tapering off to $0 during the 2019 - 2022 plan year.
